rules.rule: INSERT REPORT on a function-group include (e.g. LYFPAYMU19) DESTROYS the FUPARAREF interface metadata for the function modules in that include. After every INSERT REPORT on such an include, ALWAYS execute `GENERATE REPORT '<FUNCTION_GROUP>'` (e.g. SAPLYFPAYM) in the same one-shot to repopulate FUPARAREF.
rules.why: Session #073 (2026-05-09): deployed Y_FI_DMEE_ADR v2 via INSERT REPORT on LYFPAYMU19. The FM source updated correctly (REPOSRC R3STATE='A'), but FUPARAREF returned TABLE_WITHOUT_DATA — interface metadata was wiped. Symptoms: RPY_FUNCTIONMODULE_READ_NEW returns 0 lines; DMEE editor reports DMEE_ABA358 'incorrect interface'; FM may execute partially (cached compiled code) or fail silently per call. The fix was an explicit `GENERATE REPORT 'SAPLYFPAYM'` which restored 11 FUPARAREF rows from the `*"` interface comments in the source.
rules.how_to_apply:
Whenever updating a function-module body via INSERT REPORT on its include:
1. INSERT REPORT 'L<FG>U<NN>' FROM lt_src DIRECTORY ENTRY ls_trdir.
2. COMMIT WORK.
3. GENERATE REPORT 'SAPL<FG>' MESSAGE lv_msg.
4. Verify: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fupararef WHERE funcname='Y_xxx' — should be > 0.
5. If still empty, the GENERATE failed silently — investigate before assuming the FM is OK.
The RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN one-shot must include both INSERT and GENERATE in one program so they execute under the same transaction.

rules.rule: `GENERATE REPORT '<FG>'` regenerates the function-group code BUT does NOT re-parse the `*"` interface comments to update existing FUPARAREF rows. To change a parameter's pass-by-reference flag (VALUE→REFERENCE or vice versa), you must `UPDATE fupararef SET reference='X' WHERE funcname=... AND parameter=...` directly via ABAP one-shot, then GENERATE again.
rules.why: Session #073 (2026-05-09): edited Y_FI_DMEE_ADR `*"` comments to change `VALUE(I_EXTENSION)` → `REFERENCE(I_EXTENSION)` (matching DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_EXTEND_ABA). Deployed via INSERT REPORT + GENERATE REPORT. FUPARAREF still showed `reference=' '` (blank=VALUE) for I_EXTENSION. DMEE_ABA358 errors persisted. Fix: explicit UPDATE fupararef SET reference='X' WHERE funcname='Y_FI_DMEE_ADR' AND parameter='I_EXTENSION'. Then re-GENERATE. The errors disappeared.
rules.how_to_apply:
When changing FM interface in `*"` comments (pass-by-value vs reference, optional flag, type, structure):
1. Edit the source `*"` comments and INSERT REPORT.
2. GENERATE REPORT '<FG>' (regenerates code but NOT FUPARAREF flags).
3. SELECT * FROM fupararef WHERE funcname='Y_xxx' — verify each parameter's `reference`, `optional`, `structure` matches the new comments.
4. For any mismatch, UPDATE fupararef SET <flag>='<new>' WHERE funcname=... AND parameter=...
5. COMMIT WORK + GENERATE REPORT '<FG>' again.
6. Re-verify FUPARAREF and run the FM via SE37 or actual caller to confirm.
Key FUPARAREF columns: PARAMETER, PARAMTYPE (I/E/C/T), STRUCTURE, OPTIONAL, REFERENCE, PPOSITION, R3STATE.

rules.rule: DMEE exit function modules (those configured as MP_EXIT_FUNC in DMEE_TREE_NODE) MUST have an interface that EXACTLY matches one of the two SAP templates: DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_ABA (legacy) or DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_EXTEND_ABA (modern, with REFERENCE(I_EXTENSION)). Any deviation triggers DMEE_ABA358 'function module XXX has incorrect interface' and the tree validation refuses to compile.
rules.why: Session #073 (2026-05-09): Y_FI_DMEE_ADR had `VALUE(I_EXTENSION)` while DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_EXTEND_ABA has `REFERENCE(I_EXTENSION)`. The mismatch produced 8 DMEE_ABA358 errors (one per Dbtr/PstlAdr/* leaf assigned to Y_FI_DMEE_ADR). Runtime sometimes tolerates the mismatch (executes with a cached compile), but tree-editor validation, transport activation, and Test mode all reject. Strict-match is enforced field-by-field in FUPARAREF: parameter name, paramtype (I/E/C/T), structure, reference flag, optional flag, position.
rules.how_to_apply:
Before assigning a custom FM as a DMEE node exit:
1. SELECT * FROM fupararef WHERE funcname='DMEE_EXIT_TEMPLATE_EXTEND_ABA' (the reference).
2. SELECT * FROM fupararef WHERE funcname='<your custom FM>'.
3. Diff the two: every field — PARAMETER, PARAMTYPE, STRUCTURE, OPTIONAL, REFERENCE, PPOSITION — must match.
4. If mismatch, fix via INSERT REPORT (source comments) + UPDATE fupararef (reference flag) + GENERATE REPORT.
5. Test by running tx DMEE → tree → Validate / Test active version. Should be zero DMEE_ABA358.
Reference template (extended): `IMPORTING VALUE(I_TREE_TYPE) TYPE DMEE_TREETYPE_ABA, VALUE(I_TREE_ID) TYPE DMEE_TREEID_ABA, VALUE(I_ITEM), VALUE(I_PARAM), VALUE(I_UPARAM), REFERENCE(I_EXTENSION) TYPE DMEE_EXIT_INTERFACE_ABA. EXPORTING REFERENCE(O_VALUE), REFERENCE(C_VALUE), REFERENCE(N_VALUE), REFERENCE(P_VALUE). TABLES I_TAB.`

rules.rule: Every piece of code we extract from SAP (ABAP source via RPY_PROGRAM_READ, function modules, classes, includes, enhancements, BAdI implementations, BTEs) is BRAIN DATA — not transient artifacts. It must be persisted under extracted_code/<DOMAIN>/<SUBDOMAIN>/, registered in brain_v2 (annotations, claims, knowledge_docs), and linked in brain_state.json so future agents can: (1) understand how SAP works at UNESCO, (2) detect patterns across modules, (3) discover connections between elements and domains, (4) avoid re-extracting the same code, (5) audit historical SAP behavior.
rules.why: User directive Session #073 (2026-05-09): 'Y las bajadas de codigo son datos que deben estar en el brain para conocer como funciona SAP luego los agentes determinan patrones y conexiones entre elementos y domains'. The raison d'etre of the brain v2 backbone (rule feedback_brain_code_tables_are_backbone) is that programs+tables+config are the SAP system, and edges between them are the intelligence. Extracted code is the only way to make those edges concrete (code → reads_table → joins_with). If extracted code only lives as one-off files outside the brain, every analysis starts from scratch. Concrete pain Session #073: while studying Nicolas's YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_FALLBACK / FR / DE / IT / UTIL classes, I discovered a sophisticated PPC-customizing pattern (YTFI_PPC_TAG + YTFI_PPC_STRUC + T015L driven by util class constructor) that should be a brain-level annotation visible to every future incident touching DMEE — otherwise the next agent re-discovers it from scratch.
rules.how_to_apply:
On every code extraction:
1. Save source under extracted_code/<DOMAIN>/<SUBDOMAIN>/<NAME>.abap (e.g. extracted_code/FI/DMEE_p01_canonical/YCL_IDFI_CGI_DMEE_FALLBACK====CM001.abap).
2. For each new object: add an annotation to brain_v2/annotations/annotations.json with finding (1-2 sentences of what the code does), tag, flavor, related_objects, evidence_tier=TIER_1 source code, line numbers if specific.
3. For patterns spanning multiple objects: write a knowledge doc under knowledge/domains/<DOMAIN>/ and link it from the relevant brain_state.objects[X].knowledge_docs.
4. For author/team-ownership: capture in annotation 'author' field (e.g. 'N_MENARD') so future agents respect feedback_only_modify_our_own_code.
5. Run brain_v2/rebuild_all.py at session close to refresh brain_state.json.
6. Cross-reference: when extracting object X, check brain_state.objects[X] first — if already annotated, only add new findings, do not duplicate.
7. NEVER let extracted_code/ rot — it is a first-class persistence layer of the project.

rules.rule: Rule: when emitting a vendor address from any UNESCO output (DMEE, avisos, F110 confirms, BCM print, treasury report), check PA0006 SUBTY='1' BEFORE reading ADRC.STREET. Cast LIFNR → PERNR via NUMC(8). If PA0006 hits → employee path (real home address). If not → vendor path (ADRC). The dispatch is KTOKK-agnostic — explicit KTOKK='SCSA' branching (the v5 design) misses cases where staff are paid against KTOKK=UNES / INDV / ICVS LIFNRs.
rules.why: Session #073 (2026-05-08): Y_FI_DMEE_ADR v5 used explicit KTOKK='SCSA' detection. F110 SEPA run for Simona BERTOLDINI emitted 'BFM/FAS/PAY' as <StrtNm> because her payment LIFNR is KTOKK=UNES (not SCSA), so v5 fell through to ADRC and printed the dept code. v6 PA0006-first detection is robust regardless of which KTOKK F110 paid against. Validated live on D01 V01T3 run — BERTOLDINI's real home address (16 avenue des Murs du Parc, 94300 Vincennes) emitted correctly. UNESCO LIFNR↔PERNR convention: PERNR = LIFNR cast NUMC(8) (e.g. 0010008305 → 10008305). ADRC.STREET stores dept codes for SCSA staff records — assuming ADRC = real address is wrong system-wide, not just SEPA-specific.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) For any new code that emits a vendor address: SELECT SINGLE FROM PA0006 WHERE PERNR = LIFNR (NUMC8 cast) AND SUBTY='1' AND date-valid first. (2) If SY-SUBRC=0 → use PA0006-STRAS/PSTLZ/ORT01/LAND1/STATE. (3) Else fall back to ADRC of the LIFNR. (4) For audit of EXISTING code: grep for SELECT * FROM ADRC patterns where the addrnumber comes from LIFNR-related sources (LFA1-ADRNR, FPAYH-ZADNR, etc.) — every such site is a candidate for the same bug. (5) Document the convention in the affected output's spec / companion. (6) Reference: Y_FI_DMEE_ADR v6 in extracted_code/FI/DMEE_full_inventory/Y_FI_DMEE_ADR_v6.abap; knowledge/domains/Payment/vendor_address_routing_by_ktokk.md.

rules.rule: Before claiming a custom FM (e.g. Y_FI_DMEE_ADR) fixes a payment-format bug, query DMEE_TREE_NODE.MP_EXIT_FUNC for every relevant tree to confirm the FM is actually wired. A fix only applies where the tree calls it.
rules.why: Session #074: I initially extended the v6 simulator across all SEPA formats — but Y_FI_DMEE_ADR is wired ONLY in /SEPA_CT_UNES. The drift forecast for /SEPA_CT_ICTP_* was theoretical (would-happen-if), not in-scope. User caught this: 'no cambien nunca estos formatos cómo puede ser que funcione'. The same logic applies to /CGI_XML_CT_UNESCO and /CITI/XML/UNESCO/DC_V3_01 — they wire FI_CGI_DMEE_EXIT_W_BADI and /CITIPMW/* FMs, not Y_FI_DMEE_ADR. The fix surface is bounded by tree wiring, not by FM availability.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) For any payment-format bug claim, query DMEE_TREE_NODE for the affected leaves with MP_EXIT_FUNC populated. (2) Separate 'in-scope' (FM is wired) from 'theoretical' (FM would fix if wired). (3) When reporting drift across formats, label each row as IN-SCOPE or OUT-OF-SCOPE based on tree wiring evidence, not on assumed coverage. (4) Reference: extracted DMEE_TREE_NODE topology for the 5 active formats in claim 185.

rules.rule: DFPAYG (execution evidence) and DFPAYV (config matrix) are the canonical source for any 'which payment format/run/vendor' question. Always cross-reference both before answering scope or coverage questions about UNESCO payments.
rules.why: Session #074 added both tables to Gold DB. DFPAYG = 9,848 rows = ground truth for what actually fired in the last 2 years; DFPAYV = 84 rows = static config showing what CAN fire (with 6 lapsed configs that never run). Combined with REGUH, they let SQL answer: 'which staff vendor was paid via which format×cocode×bank×account×PM combination?' — replacing ad-hoc P01 RFC queries.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) Format scope questions: SELECT DISTINCT FORMI FROM DFPAYG WHERE LAUFD >= '<window>' (= active set); SELECT FORMI FROM DFPAYV (= configured set); difference = lapsed configs. (2) Vendor questions: JOIN DFPAYG to REGUH on (LAUFD, LAUFI, ZBUKR) to get the vendor list paid via each format. (3) Bank/account/PM granularity: REGUH_FAST has HBKID, HKTID, RZAWE — better than DFPAYG for the routing breakdown. (4) Indexes: idx_reguh_run on (LAUFD,LAUFI,ZBUKR), idx_dfpayg_formi, idx_dfpayg_zbukr.

rules.rule: When reporting payment metrics, ALWAYS label whether the count is 'distinct LIFNRs' or 'REGUH payment lines'. Same employee paid 30 times = 1 distinct LIFNR = 30 lines. The two scales differ by 5-30x in typical UNESCO data.
rules.why: Session #074 user clarification: 'O sea son la cantidades de pagos staff que se hacen para ese formato' — user assumed 'staff drift = number of payments' but my number was 'distinct staff vendors'. The actual XMLs emitted = REGUH lines, not vendors. For /SEPA_CT_UNES UNES 2025-26: 1,659 staff vendors but 12,107 lines (7.3x factor).
rules.how_to_apply: (1) Default to BOTH counts when reporting: e.g. '1,659 staff vendors → 12,107 lines'. (2) For business impact (XMLs emitted with wrong data, bank rejection volume), use LINES. (3) For root-cause analysis (which employees are affected), use VENDORS. (4) Include the multiplier explicitly: 'pays/vendor ratio = 7.3x'.

rules.rule: When presenting tables to operational users, use the FULL business name for each column (Company Code, House Bank, Bank Account, Payment Method) — NOT the SAP technical abbreviation (ZBUKR, HBKID, HKTID, RZAWE) or my shorthand (COCO, BANK, ACCT, PM).
rules.why: Session #074 user feedback: 'O faltan las columnas, Company code, house bank bank Account, and mediunm payment please' — when I used abbreviated headers, the user explicitly asked for the full names. Treasury and finance operators read SAP tables every day but the technical names slow them down vs business labels.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) First column header row uses business names: 'Company Code (ZBUKR)' is acceptable, 'ZBUKR' alone is not. (2) Apply consistently across companions and brain output. (3) Exception: when the audience is purely technical (ABAP devs / brain agents), abbreviations are fine.

rules.rule: RFC_READ_TABLE has narrow accepted OPTIONS syntax: (a) NO 'IN (...)' clauses — use multiple single-field calls instead; (b) leading space required when concatenating conditions (' AND TECH_NAME = ...'); (c) DATA_BUFFER_EXCEEDED on wide tables — limit FIELDS to <20 columns or expect 512-byte WA truncation. Document tables that are DMEE_TREE_NODE, REGUH, etc. often hit these limits.
rules.why: Session #074 wasted ~15 minutes debugging OPTION_NOT_VALID errors when querying DMEE_TREE_NODE with IN clauses. Once switched to per-TECH_NAME calls in a loop, queries worked. This is a recurring pattern across sessions but never captured as a rule.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) When OPTION_NOT_VALID appears, simplify OPTIONS: one condition per row, leading space on continuation rows, no IN clauses. (2) For multi-value filtering, loop the query per value instead. (3) When DATA_BUFFER_EXCEEDED hits, narrow FIELDS list or split into multiple narrow queries. (4) Verified working pattern: OPTIONS=[{'TEXT':"TREE_ID = '/X'"}, {'TEXT':" AND TECH_NAME = 'StrtNm'"}]. Bad: OPTIONS=[{'TEXT':"TREE_ID='/X' AND TECH_NAME IN ('StrtNm','BldgNb')"}].

rules.rule: When SAP auth fails, ALWAYS test the same credentials via both RFC (port 3300) AND HTTP (port 80) before declaring 'password is wrong'. SAP commonly accepts the same user/password on one protocol while rejecting it on another — caused by SU01 user type, USR02 password-buffer desync, or SICF policy. Run the 60-second diagnostic in unescrp/.claude/skills/sap-fiori-react-builder/sap-fiori-react-builder/references/deployment/sap-d01-connection-patterns.md before opening a credentials INC.
rules.why: Session #075: unescrp project burned 2+ hours assuming the 40-char password was stale, including retrying passwords found in earlier .env snapshots and probing /sap/bc/adt/discovery 6 times. The same password authenticates cleanly via RFC. Root cause is SAP-side ICF/SU01 — none of the client-side fixes would have helped. Isolating protocol vs credentials would have saved the time and triggered the correct BASIS ticket immediately.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) First failure to authenticate → run RFC probe (pyrfc T000 read). (2) If RFC works → it's not the password; switch to HTTP probe (urllib Basic + ADT discovery). (3) If RFC fails → check .env / VPN / SNC config. (4) If RFC works AND HTTP fails → SAP-side, open BASIS ticket with the diagnostic evidence. Don't keep trying passwords. (5) Document the result in the project's connection-patterns reference file.

rules.rule: Do NOT trust `sap_adt_client.fetch_csrf()` or any `_request()` call as proof of HTTP auth success. The current `_request` implementation catches `urllib.error.HTTPError` and returns `(status, body, headers)` without raising — and SAP echoes a CSRF token even on 401 when `X-CSRF-Token: Fetch` is sent. Always assert `status == 200` after the call. Patch `_request()` to raise on 4xx, or replace the client with one that propagates errors.
rules.why: Session #075: I told the user 'ADT HTTP works' based on `fetch_csrf()` returning normally, then realized the client silently swallowed the 401 and returned an empty token. The mistake cost trust and required a public correction. The bug has likely caused false positives in other sessions where ADT 'success' messages preceded mysterious downstream failures.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) When calling sap_adt_client methods, check the returned status code explicitly, not just whether a value came back. (2) Add a fix to `_request`: `if status >= 400: raise HTTPError(...)`. (3) Same patch needed for fetch_csrf, search_object, get_source, etc. (4) Until patched, run a separate `urllib.request.urlopen` probe to confirm 200 before trusting the client.

rules.rule: When another project (Tier 2 application or sibling Tier 1) consumes this brain, SAP-system facts (tables, transactions, standard customizing, customer customizing in any SAP module) MUST live ONLY in abapobjectscreation/brain_v2. The consuming project cites by reference (path + node id) and never duplicates. Project-specific facts (Z objects the consumer is building, design decisions, application-internal taxonomy) live in the consumer's brain.
rules.why: Session #00 of FINCLOSSING (2026-05-23) — first Tier 2 application project that needs to consume SAP truth without forking it. Without this rule, two brains will diverge on facts like 'BKPF columns' or 'CLOCO table layout' and the failure mode (silent drift) is invisible until an agent makes a wrong decision against a stale copy. Plausibility-without-evidence (CP-003 violation) is the concrete failure pattern.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) Before writing a fact to a consumer's brain, ask: 'is this about SAP itself, or about what the consumer is BUILDING?' (2) If about SAP → grep abapobjectscreation/brain_v2 first; if missing, ADD it to abapobjectscreation, not the consumer. (3) If about the consumer's Z objects / design / app-internal taxonomy → consumer's brain is correct. (4) Each consumer maintains a `refs_external.json` listing every layer/file it reads from this brain — that is the canonical drift-detection surface. (5) Reverse pointer: this brain maintains `brain_v2/consumers.md` listing every project that depends on it, so refactors here check downstream impact.

rules.rule: When prior analysis has converged on an obvious recommended path AND the user signals agreement (OK/si/dale/proceed), do NOT present a 3-option AskUserQuestion menu. Execute the recommendation directly. The agent OWNS the technical decision.
rules.why: During session #076 ADT expansion, after a long analysis that converged on Build now + BASIS ticket in parallel, I still presented a 3-option menu. User rejected the tool use and said OK proceed im not sure what you need from basis. Menus are friction when path is obvious. Reinforces existing rule feedback_own_the_decision_stop_asking.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. If my prior message ended with clear recommendation + user agrees (OK/si/dale/proceed), do not present options. Execute.
2. Reserve AskUserQuestion for genuinely-equivalent-tradeoff cases or when user has not yet given any signal.
3. When the user signals lack of context (not sure what X means), do NOT ask them to choose - give them what they need or just decide for them and explain.
4. If I find myself drafting an AskUserQuestion after a long analysis, delete it and proceed.

rules.rule: Before recommending any SAP capability (ADT endpoint, BAPI, RFC FM, transaction availability), VERIFY it exists on the target kernel via empirical probe. SAP NetWeaver capabilities differ across releases - what works in S/4HANA / NW 7.5x may be 404 on UNESCO ECC 6.0 EhP8 (NW 7.40). Never assume kernel-uniform.
rules.why: Session #076 violation: I confidently recommended ADT REST define_table / create_index as the canonical DDIC path, including copy-paste prompts for the parallel unescrp conversation. Then user tested empirically and confirmed /sap/bc/adt/ddic/tables returns HTTP 404 on D01 (NW 7.40) - endpoint shipped in NW 7.50. ~400 lines of code became S/4HANA scaffolding, cross-project recommendation had to be retracted before being applied.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. Before recommending an ADT method, call adt_discovery() and grep the response for the relevant collection. If endpoint absent, the method will 404 - recommend RFC alternative instead.
2. Before recommending a BAPI / RFC FM, run RFC_READ_TABLE FROM TFDIR WHERE FUNCNAME EQ name to confirm availability.
3. Before recommending a transaction, verify via TSTCT or quick GUI probe.
4. UNESCO landscape baseline: ECC 6.0 EhP8 = NW 7.40. Treat any capability described as NW 7.5+ or S/4HANA-only as unavailable until proven otherwise.
5. When recommending a path that crosses kernel versions, be explicit about version requirement IN THE RECOMMENDATION.
6. When a recommendation is later proven wrong by empirical evidence, revise the related memory rules IMMEDIATELY and acknowledge the error directly - no softening.

rules.rule: For ANY new ABAP/DDIC object work (create table, DE, domain, class, program, FM, index, etc.), the agent works EXCLUSIVELY in D01. NEVER touches P01 - not for write, not for read, not for preflight, not for does this exist. The only legitimate P01 read in a creation context is post-transport verification.
rules.why: Session #076 violation: I called from_env(P01) and ran RFC_READ_TABLE FROM DD02L WHERE TABNAME='ZCRP_CERTHEAD' to triple-confirm the table doesn't exist there. The check was logically unnecessary - by the transport model, if it doesn't exist in D01 it cannot exist in P01 - and crossed a boundary the user explicitly maintains. User response in CAPS: PARA NUEVOS OBJETOS LO HACEMOS EN D01!!! NUNCA P01. This rule is STRICTER than the broader no-prod-writes rule.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. When the user mentions creating/modifying/deploying a new ABAP/DDIC object: pin the system as D01 only. Do not call from_env(P01).
2. For preflight of objects related to a new creation, query D01 only.
3. The only legitimate P01 read in a new-object context is post-transport verification - prefer STMS over RFC.
4. If user explicitly requests a P01 probe for some OTHER reason (incident, data extraction, customizing read), that is allowed under standard no-prod-writes rule.
5. If unsure whether request is new-object work or diagnosis work, ASK before touching P01.

rules.rule: ADT-first is qualified by kernel + object class. SOURCE CODE objects (PROG/CLAS/INTF/FUGR/FUNC/INCLUDE/ENHO/XSLT/BSP) - ADT-first on ALL kernels including EhP8. DDIC objects (TABL/DTEL/DOMA/INDX) - ADT-first ONLY on NW 7.50+ / S/4HANA. On EhP8 (UNESCO D01/P01) DDIC creation MUST use the DDIF wrapper (sap_adt_client.define_table_via_ddif / define_data_element_via_ddif / define_domain_via_ddif) with TR_TADIR_INTERFACE injection and verify_tadir post-check.
rules.why: Session #076: I originally saved a rule ADT-first for ALL DDIC, generating ABAP programs that call DDIF_*_PUT is forbidden as architecture. Empirical probe revealed ADT REST /sap/bc/adt/ddic/tables returns HTTP 404 on NW 7.40 - endpoint shipped in NW 7.50. So on EhP8 the DDIF_*_PUT via RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN pattern is NOT debt - it is the only path. Pain points (opaque RC=2, IN-list parser bug, TADIR-orphan) are real and mitigated by the wrapper, not avoided. The original rule overgeneralized and had to be corrected.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. Before any DDIC create/modify, call adt_discovery() once and grep for the endpoint. If absent, fall back to the DDIF wrapper (NEVER to ad-hoc programs without preflight + TADIR fix).
2. For SOURCE CODE work, default to ADT REST.
3. When reviewing legacy projects for RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN + DDIF_*_PUT patterns on EhP8, do NOT mark them as debt - verify they implement preflight + TR_TADIR_INTERFACE + structured-error mitigation. If they do, the pattern is correct; if not, refactor to the wrapper, do not switch to ADT (which would fail).
4. Track the S/4HANA migration: when UNESCO upgrades, flip DDIC operations to the ADT methods (already scaffolded) - field-list and return-dict shape are identical.
5. DDIC creation order (both paths): Domain - Data Element - Table - Index. Validate prerequisites before each create.

rules.rule: CRITICAL HARD RULE: NEVER modify, alter, extend the structure of, append fields to, change DEs of, or alter activation state of SAP-delivered standard objects. Applies to ALL tools (DDIF wrapper, ADT REST, abapGit pull, RFC FM calls, Playwright). Only Z*/Y*/customer-namespace objects can be modified. For SAP-standard extension needs, use append structures, customer includes, BAdIs, enhancement implementations, or user exits — never modify the original. Refuse the request and explain when asked to modify a standard object.
rules.why: SAP licensing forbids unauthorized modification of delivered objects (SSCR keys required); upgrades (SPS/EhP/S/4HANA conversion) overwrite standard objects and force SPDD/SPAU manual adjustments which are manual, error-prone, and break frequently. UNESCO ECC 6.0 EhP8 is a mature production estate where standard modifications carry ongoing maintenance cost on every Support Package application — UNESCO BASIS team will refuse them on principle. Modifying a standard DE/domain cascades activation to thousands of dependent tables. A wrong TR_TADIR_INTERFACE call against a standard object can set EDTFLAG=X and break SE11 editability system-wide.
rules.how_to_apply:
Before any DDIC/code write: check if object name is non-standard.

  def is_standard(name): return not name.upper().startswith(('Z','Y','/'))

If standard, REFUSE the call and respond:
  1. Cite this rule (feedback_never_modify_standard_objects)
  2. Explain why (SAP licensing + upgrade safety + UNESCO policy)
  3. Offer permitted alternative (append structure / customer include / BAdI / enhancement)
  4. Ask user to rephrase as Z-namespace addition

Permitted alternatives:
  - Add fields to standard table: Z append structure (CI_* include or .APPEND)
  - Modify standard FM behavior: BAdI / enhancement spot / user exit (Z implementation)
  - Modify standard class behavior: ENHO enhancement implementation
  - Customizing of standard T-tables: SM30 row CRUD = DATA changes (permitted), structure changes (forbidden)

Edge cases:
  - Customizing rows in T-tables: data changes are OK, structure changes are NOT
  - PFCG role modifications: copy to Z-named role first
  - SICF service activation: flag toggle OK; handler class modification NOT

rules.rule: ARCHITECTURAL STANDARD: abapGit is the DEFAULT deployment path for any object type it supports (170+ types covering DDIC, source code, enhancements, OData, BSP). DDIF wrapper / ADT REST / RFC alternatives are BRIDGES or FALLBACKS for cases abapGit cannot cover OR for the period until abapGit is installed on the target system. Priority order: 1) abapGit (default for supported types when installed), 2) ADT REST (source code on all kernels, bridge for source until abapGit), 3) DDIF wrapper (DDIC on EhP8, bridge until abapGit), 4) RFC/Playwright (for objects no other tool covers: SM59, SM30 rows, SICF, RZ10, BOR, PFCG user assignments).
rules.why: abapGit is the de-facto industry standard for SAP Z code deployment: 10+ years, 50K+ installs, SAP-promoted via TechEd. It handles TADIR/CTS architecturally correctly (uses RS_CORR_INSERT, no EDTFLAG bug), provides native version control with Git history/blame/diff/rollback, supports atomic multi-object deploys (N objects in 1 ZIP = 1 TR), is forward-compatible across kernels (EhP8/NW 7.5x/S/4HANA), enables cross-system sync (D01->QAS without STMS forward path), and supports PR-based code review. The DDIF wrapper we built is a hand-rolled subset that learned the same lessons through bugs (TADIR-orphan, EDTFLAG poisoning) that abapGit solves by design. Installation operational state (installed or not) is separate from architectural correctness (abapGit IS the standard regardless).
rules.how_to_apply:
When proposing a deployment: lead with "if abapGit is installed, use it; otherwise the bridge is X". Don't propose the bridge as the default.

When abapGit is not installed (current D01 state): include the BASIS ticket escalation in the response, marked STRATEGIC PRIORITY (not optional). Bridge solution is temporary.

When designing new automation: API shape compatible with both backends (e.g. define_table(...) works whether backend is abapGit-pull or DDIF wrapper). Forward-compatible.

When migrating to S/4HANA: abapGit path stays. DDIF wrapper deprecates. ADT REST takes over what DDIF did, but abapGit lifecycle features remain its own value.

When auditing legacy projects (unescrp, ecosystem): check if they use abapGit. If yes, validate they're using it correctly. If no, propose migration when timing allows.

Before recommending abapGit as the immediate path: verify install via 5-way TADIR/TRDIR/TDEVC/TFDIR probe (per feedback_verify_capabilities_before_recommending). If not installed, recommend bridge with STRATEGIC install ticket attached.

rules.rule: When assessing whether a SAP data-access restriction (note, patch, audit, security advisory) affects us, FIRST read our code to classify the EXACT function-module / API family our pipeline calls, then compare it against the SPECIFIC API the restriction names. Never reason from the category ('it is an RFC that reads data'). ODP Data Replication APIs (RODPS_REPL_*, ODQ_*, /SAPDS/) are a different framework from the generic RFC_READ_TABLE reader. UNESCO's Gold DB uses RFC_READ_TABLE only and is OUT OF SCOPE of SAP Note 3255746; the 2026-06-09 ODP-blocking patch does not affect it.
rules.why: SAP Note 3255746 ('Unpermitted usage of ODP Data Replication APIs') triggered an 'are we affected?' question. The failure mode is reasoning from the category: assuming any data-extraction RFC is in scope. ODP is a replication framework (delta queues, subscriptions, change-data-capture); RFC_READ_TABLE is a generic single-table SELECT-equivalent with no delta queue and no subscription. Conflating them produces either a false 'we are non-compliant' panic or -- worse -- a false 'we are safe' on a note that DID hit us. Precision on the exact API IS the whole answer (CP-003: precision + evidence + facts).
rules.how_to_apply:
1) Grep the repo for the SPECIFIC restricted FMs/namespaces named in the note (e.g. RODPS_REPL, ODQ_, /SAPDS/) -- report the call count with file:line.
2) Identify the FM our pipeline actually calls (read rfc_helpers.py / extract_*.py) and cite it.
3) Produce a restricted-vs-used comparison so the verdict is auditable.
4) Recommend running SAP's own self-assessment tool (when the note ships one, e.g. Note 3439624) to convert code evidence into SAP-sourced confirmation.
5) If the pipeline depends on a single non-released FM (RFC_READ_TABLE), flag it as a forward-looking risk and name the SAP-endorsed durable path (ODP-OData / Business Data Cloud).

rules.rule: No research/analysis produces conclusions or plans until it is CLOSED. A research is CLOSED only when ALL 8 guarantees pass: (1) completeness, (2) graded sources, (3) adversarial verification finished, (4) citable evidence per claim, (5) explicit confidence tier, (6) gaps stated as open questions, (7) reproducibility, (8) no-spin attestation. An incomplete/stopped/failed run is OPEN -> discard or re-run; NEVER salvage its fragments into findings. Conclusions and plans are built ONLY on CLOSED claims, each carrying its tier + citation; anything on a LOW/open item is labeled ASSUMPTION/RISK.
rules.why: s079: I presented unverified scraps from a deep research that died in Fetch (no Verify/Synthesize) as Phase-1 findings. User: 'mentiroso o irresponsable... si fuera algo medico que te parece usar un research de este nivel'. Quality discipline must be a STANDING gate, not a doc I write reactively. This is table-stakes, not a discovery.
rules.how_to_apply: Before using ANY research output: confirm it reached Synthesize (web research = Verify(3-vote)+Synthesize ran; own analysis = each claim has path:line/query-result + tier). If not closed: say so directly, re-run, invent nothing. Label every presented item VERIFIED / INFERRED / NOT-ESTABLISHED. Do not launch web-dependent research while internet is flagged down. Phase A (close research) strictly precedes Phase B (conclusions/plans). Full spec: knowledge/research_closing_methodology.md.

rules.rule: Every domain is modeled as a PAIR — AS-DESIGNED (standard SAP) + AS-RUN (our process) — and scored across 9 capability dimensions (S_STANDARD_REF, A_PROCESS, B_CODE, C_CONFIG, D_DATA, E_AUTH, F_INTERFACE_FILE, G_CONFORMANCE=the delta, H_IMPROVE). This domain×capability matrix (Layer 15, brain_v2/capability_model/) IS the operating model. Work is SELECTED by querying `graph_queries.py capability_gaps` — the roadmap is generated, not written. Empty COLUMNS are systemic model gaps, not per-domain. The model is PORTABLE across projects (unesco-sap-brain etc.): standard AS-DESIGNED baselines are system-invariant and shared cross-project; AS-RUN deltas are project-specific and fed back to a shared library.
rules.why: s079: the process+code+conformance work is crucial to the MODEL, not a one-off plan. User: 'cómo lo reflejamos más allá del plan... los dominios deben ALINEARSE y luego AMPLIARSE'. A plan is consumed and archived; a model axis is queried and grows. Reflecting it structurally (4th axis) makes acquired knowledge align to one skeleton and makes every gap a deterministic, ranked work item.
rules.how_to_apply: At session start, read brain_state.capability_model. Before proposing work, run `graph_queries.py capability_gaps` and pick from the ranked expansion_order. When a domain is touched (incident/claim/companion), update its capability cell. A capability is fully met only when BOTH strata exist AND the G delta is computed. Never present an AS-RUN finding as conformance without the AS-DESIGNED baseline (S_STANDARD_REF precondition). Keep the matrix honest: ●HAVE/◐PARTIAL/○NONE per cell with evidence. Full spec: knowledge/capability_model.md.

rules.rule: Every CLOSED deep-research is archived under brain_v2/research/ (full result + sources + findings). Before launching ANY new deep-research, DEDUPE against brain_v2/research/sources_index.json (91 urls already read) and findings_registry.json (37 verified + 26 refuted). Do NOT re-fetch a source already analyzed or re-litigate a verified/refuted claim — READ the archive. Scope new runs to ENRICH the named openQuestions, not to repeat. Append, never overwrite. A FAILED/degraded run is logged in _run_log.json and superseded by a solo rerun — never re-run the same degraded query.
rules.why: s079: deep-research outputs lived in EPHEMERAL temp files — they would be lost, forcing re-reads/re-runs of already-analyzed sources (waste + CP-002 violation). User: 'guarda los deep researchs para enriquecerlos en el futuro y no tener que releer algo que ya analizaste'.
rules.how_to_apply: At research time: (1) grep sources_index.json for the candidate domains/urls; (2) if covered, cite the archived finding instead of re-fetching; (3) read the target research's openQuestions and scope the new run ONLY to those gaps; (4) after a run closes, archive it via the same persist pattern (full result + update sources_index + findings_registry). Run SERIALLY (concurrency degrades Verify).

rules.rule: Distinguish TECHNICAL decisions (the agent OWNS — do not ask) from STRATEGIC/BUSINESS-REALITY decisions that only the user/org can answer and that DETERMINE SCOPE/RELEVANCE (ASK before investing). Migration strategy (brownfield vs greenfield), which systems/company-codes/domains are in scope, business priorities, chosen vendors/paths — these are org facts NOT derivable from code/data/sensible defaults. Assuming one risks wasting a whole research/build. A focused question is cheaper than discarded work.
rules.why: s079: I assumed greenfield was in scope (it was in an openQuestion) and was about to run a full RES-S4-GREENFIELD research — but UNESCO uses BROWNFIELD. The research would have been wasted. User: 'como feedback sería buena la pregunta de qué estrategia usaríamos'. This complements (does NOT contradict) own_the_decision/no_menus: own the technical HOW; ask the strategic WHICH-PATH that the org decides.
rules.how_to_apply: Before scoping a research/build whose RELEVANCE depends on a strategic choice (migration approach, in-scope systems, chosen path/vendor, business priority), check: is this a fact I can derive from code/data/defaults, or an org decision? If org decision and it changes what work is relevant -> ask ONE focused question (AskUserQuestion) first. Still own the technical HOW (no menus for implementation). The test: 'would assuming this waste consequential work if wrong?' -> if yes, ask.

rules.rule: This project HAS a persisted operating model: brain_state.capability_model (Layer 15) + brain_v2/capability_model/* + brain_v2/research/* (7 closed researches). Before proposing ANY new framework/model/layer, or redesigning brain_state.json's schema, you MUST confirm you loaded brain_state.capability_model. If you did not load it, you do not know the project state — LOAD it, do not rebuild from scratch. Re-inventing what exists is a CP-001 (traceability) + CP-002 (preserve) violation and wastes the whole prior investment.
rules.why: s079: a PARALLEL conversation re-derived the model from scratch and was about to redesign brain_state.json schema — because it skipped the brain read and the model existed ONLY in brain_state.json (not in the auto-loaded CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md). User: 'si no persiste, que valor tiene todo este trabajo, las futuras interacciones lo ignoran'. The model's existence is now announced in the auto-loaded channels (CLAUDE.md STOP block, MEMORY.md, SessionStart hook).
rules.how_to_apply: At session start the SessionStart hook + CLAUDE.md STOP block announce the model. If a task smells like 'design a model/framework/layers' for this project: STOP, load brain_state.capability_model, and EXTEND it — never replace. Schema changes to brain_state.json go through build_brain_state.py + rebuild_all.py, never hand-edits, and never from a session that hasn't loaded the current model. One session writes brain_state at a time.

rules.rule: When you BUILD a new model, layer, or persistent state, IMMEDIATELY register its EXISTENCE in the AUTO-LOADED channels (CLAUDE.md top + the lean bootstrap index + the SessionStart hook + MEMORY.md top) — at creation time, NOT at session close. A fresh conversation only knows what is auto-loaded; state saved to a read-on-demand file is invisible. Knowledge that a new session cannot FIND is worthless (CP-001/CP-002).
rules.why: s079: the capability_model lived only in brain_state.json (read-on-demand). A parallel conversation re-invented it and almost redesigned the schema because the auto-loaded CLAUDE.md/MEMORY never announced it. User: 'fue muy preocupante que no sepas'. The model was built but unfindable.
rules.how_to_apply: After creating any model/layer/major-state: (1) add a pointer at the TOP of CLAUDE.md; (2) regenerate the lean index (build_brain_index.py); (3) ensure the SessionStart hook mentions it. Treat 'persisted to its own file' as NOT DONE until the auto-loaded channels announce it. Continuity = the next session cannot miss it, not merely 'the file exists'.

rules.rule: NEVER claim 'consistent', 'complete', 'aligned', 'done', or 'they tell the same story' without FIRST running the command that proves it and showing the output. Assertion is not verification.
rules.why: s079: asserted 'the 4 artifacts tell the same story' (false — the dimension count had drifted 8 vs 10) and shipped '8 dimensions' while the model had 10. Both caught by the user: 'no sos consistente'. Violated CP-003 (claims need evidence).
rules.how_to_apply: Before any consistency/completeness/done claim: run a check (grep the count across files, diff the IDs, run the validator) and SHOW it. If you cannot run a check, say 'unverified' rather than asserting. Pair with rule #148.

rules.rule: Before hand-building INFRASTRUCTURE (memory, continuity, agent orchestration, scheduling, retrieval), CHECK what Anthropic / Claude Code / the platform ALREADY ships (Memory tool, Managed Agents + dreaming, hooks, subagents, /compact). Borrow before build. Verify via the claude-code-guide / official docs, not from memory.
rules.why: s079: hand-built a memory store + a 'dreaming' curation that Anthropic ships as Managed Agents — only realized when the USER raised it ('por algo lo sacaron y nosotros estamos inventando'). We checked our OWN files for prior work but not the platform.
rules.how_to_apply: When a task is infrastructure-shaped, first ask 'does the platform already provide this?' and verify against official docs. Adopt/borrow the native piece where it fits (we borrowed the 'dreaming' concept as a SessionStart daily curation). Document the build-vs-borrow decision (e.g. decision_managed_agents_vs_claude_code.md).

rules.rule: When a read/extract/action hits a wall, FIRST run the tool we already use empirically on the actual object, THEN conclude against the KNOWN model + hard constraints (P01 = read-only via RFC/SSO ONLY; no ADT against production; no new objects/transports in P01; Excel is never a source). Park the gap as a capability-model task and keep the SSO-readable substitute. Do NOT invent exotic channels (ADT-over-HTTP, SPNEGO/Basic-password, deploy-FM-to-prod, ADT-against-prod) — that re-litigates settled constraints and fatigues the user.
rules.why: s080 (YTFM ODESC): a STRG column was not readable by RFC_READ_TABLE. Instead of empirically testing the core tool first and parking the gap, the agent spent ~7 turns proposing ADT-over-HTTP, deploying a custom read FM to P01, asking for a P01 password, and SPNEGO/Kerberos — each one violating an ALREADY-DOCUMENTED constraint (P01 read-only, SSO/RFC-only, no ADT against prod, no new objects in P01). The user redirected 4x ("me estas fatigando", "no usabamos ADT contra produccion", "esto es un regresion") and finally pointed at how data is actually read. Same family as feedback_check_platform_before_building_infra: invented instead of grounding in what exists.
rules.how_to_apply: On any blocked read/action: (1) run the core tool (RFC_READ_TABLE over SNC SSO) on the real object and report the exact result — never assume; (2) if it cannot, state the field-type/tooling limit plainly and STOP; (3) BEFORE proposing any alternative, check the hard P01 constraints — if it touches prod, needs a password, or deploys an object, it is already ruled out, do not propose it; (4) record the gap as an execution_backlog task and keep the SSO-readable substitute (e.g. OTEXT for a STRG ODESC); (5) if the user redirects twice on the same point, re-read the relevant code/constraint instead of proposing a third variant.
rules.cp_link_reason: The established model + hard constraints ARE the project knowledge; inventing new channels sacrifices that knowledge (and the user time) for the velocity of an untested idea — a CP-001 (knowledge over velocity) violation.

rules.rule: To decide whether a piece of SAP config that GENERATES output (DMEE tree node, smartform, routing) actually RENDERS/FIRES at runtime, the real generated OUTPUT is the arbiter — not the static config tables. DMEE_TREE_COND does NOT capture node-level deactivation, so reading only the condition gives false positives. If the artifact is replayable (e.g. ZSAPFPAYM_REPLAY for DMEE), generate it and read the real output BEFORE asserting a defect or alarming.
rules.why: 2026-06-17 (DMEE structured-address forensics): I read DMEE_TREE_COND, saw node N_1531351640 condition still matched BR, and alarmed it duplicated the Dbtr PstlAdr (D-1). The real replayed BR XML showed ONE PstlAdr — node #1 was deactivated by a flag NOT in the condition table; the prior "D-1 resolved" was correct. Same session I also over-stated D-2 as a CBPR+ reject risk without checking the BR flow is DOMESTIC (no impact). The real output / the business context were the evidence, not the tree read.
rules.how_to_apply: (1) Before claiming a DMEE/form node fires or suppresses, check for a deactivation/render flag OUTSIDE the condition table; if unsure, replay and read the real output. (2) Distinguish a DEAD-CONSTANT gate (e.g. UBISO=SE, a value that never occurs -> always suppresses = real bug) from a DYNAMIC exit-computed gate (e.g. -PstlAdr_More_Nodes overflow flag -> benign, emits for normal data). (3) Before asserting CBPR+/compliance reject risk, confirm the flow is cross-border SWIFT, not domestic local-clearing. (4) Update immediately and without defensiveness when real output contradicts a config-read claim.
rules.cp_link_reason: Asserting runtime behavior from a config/condition read without the generated output is approximation without measuring; the real output IS the verifiable evidence.

rules.rule: Knowledge discovered during a working conversation is NOT captured until it lives in a central store the next session auto-loads or can query (enhancement registry, claims.json, incidents.json, a domain doc, the capability_model, or feedback_rules.json). A summary in the chat is volatile and is lost when context rolls. Before session close, promote every durable, evidenced fact to its home store; the brain-steward agent owns this and is the mechanization of it.
rules.why: 2026-06-20 (BCM-signature custom code): a session fully analyzed WS90000003 / YBSEG_REL (raw UPDATE bseg SET zlspr=W) / the reject BAdI Z_CL_BNK_BADI_PAYMT_CHG, but it lived ONLY in the Treasury design doc + Golden DB and was MISSING from the master sap_custom_enhancement_registry.md until the USER noticed and asked for it. Relying on a human to notice missing central knowledge is the exact failure mode CP-001 (knowledge over velocity) exists to prevent. brain_v2/curate.py already named this as deferred future work (the transcript-pattern-extraction half of dreaming).
rules.how_to_apply: (1) At session close (or on demand "steward check"), invoke the brain-steward agent: harvest new/corrected durable facts, classify each to its home store, dedupe (latest-wins, supersede not delete), promote with evidence path + tier + cross-link, then run python brain_v2/curate.py and confirm coverage did not drop. (2) Apply the cross-reference rule: grep the entity across ALL companions/reports, fix every stale ref. (3) If the same class of knowledge keeps escaping to chat, mechanize the capture (hook/skill), do not add another prose reminder (one-in-one-out). (4) Route incidents to incident-analyst; never duplicate its 7-step job.
rules.cp_link_reason: Losing traceability is irreversible; leaving evidenced knowledge in volatile chat sacrifices knowledge for velocity, which CP-001 forbids.

rules.rule: When analyzing SAP RFC/BAPI traffic volume or patterns, ALWAYS apply the 2-axis method: (1) PROCESS axis from the FM name mapping to a business process, AND (2) ORIGIN axis from PARAMX host/dest/user identifying the satellite system. Neither axis alone is sufficient. A MuleSoft call and an internal report call to the same FM look identical without the ORIGIN axis. Coverage target: >90% of RFC volume explained.
rules.why: Discovered s085: applying only 1 axis left 80.6% of external traffic unexplained or misattributed. The 2-axis engine explained 91.1% of business RFC volume. Without ORIGIN, MuleSoft's 1.62M calls would be labeled 'unknown internal'. CP-003 precision.
rules.how_to_apply: Use process_mining/rfc_process_classifier.py (the engine). First classify by PARAM3 FM name -> process. Then enrich with PARAMX host/dest/user -> satellite/origin. Report as (process, origin) pairs. The 8.9% unexplained = known_unknowns, not a failure.

rules.rule: When a tcode-based activity count for a domain is near zero, DO NOT conclude the process is inactive. The channel may be RFC/BAPI (invisible to tcode analysis). Always cross-validate with the RESULT side (CDHDR change documents, which are channel-agnostic -- every write is captured regardless of channel) before concluding a process runs at low volume.
rules.why: Discovered s085: vendor master tcode count was ~0, suggesting MDM was idle. CDHDR showed KRED=143K change docs, dominantly dialog XK02 (M_AYIMBA 72K) + secondary ZBAPI_VENDOR_CHANGE (MP_ANCUTA 19K). The tcode-only view was a blind spot. CP-003: conclusion must be grounded in evidence from the correct source.
rules.how_to_apply: Step 1: check rsau_audit_history SLGTC for the domain tcode. Step 2 if low: query cdhdr_history WHERE OBJECTCLAS = <relevant class> GROUP BY USERNAME, TCODE, YEAR(UDATE). Step 3: the TCODE column in CDHDR shows the channel (blank=RFC, populated=dialog). Cross-classify with rsau FM stream for the full picture.

rules.rule: ALWAYS filter out JP_LOPEZ (and P_LUVHIMBI) RFC calls BEFORE reporting any RFC volume metrics from rsau_audit_history. Our own extraction is approximately 80-124K calls in a 4-month window (RFC_READ_TABLE 76K + DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET 3K + RFC_GET_FUNCTION_INTERFACE 1.5K + RSAU_API_* calls). Reporting without exclusion inflates the external-satellite share and overstates total traffic.
rules.why: Discovered s085 when reconciling RFC volumes: JP_LOPEZ RFC_READ_TABLE alone = 76,137 calls in the analysis window. Including these in 'business RFC' or 'external traffic' metrics produces systematically wrong numbers. CP-003 precision: state your own footprint before quoting volumes.
rules.how_to_apply: Add WHERE SLGUSER NOT IN ('JP_LOPEZ','P_LUVHIMBI') to all rsau_audit_history queries used for reporting satellite volumes. Document the exclusion in any claim that cites RFC volumes. The 80.6% external figure already has this exclusion applied.

rules.rule: Every actionable finding (security, control, ops, integration) must be ESCALATED as a tracked task — a PMO H-item with owner + severity + chip reference — not left as a documented note. Finding → document → MOVE ON loses the actionability.
rules.why: Born 2026-06-21 when the user caught that the write-channel SoD (E_SILVA/L_NEVES self-approve 3-way-match) and the SM21 connectivity findings were fully documented in system_operating_model_rfc.md but had never been turned into tasks. The knowledge existed only in a prose doc, not in the PMO tracker where action happens. A finding that is not escalated is knowledge that cannot be acted upon — equivalent to being lost (CP-001). Reference impl: PMO H71-H80 (.agents/intelligence/PMO_BRAIN.md) + chips task_b5d08d99 / task_995bbc03.
rules.how_to_apply: 1. After any analysis session that produces a finding with clear owner/action (SoD gap, connectivity failure, control gap, integration break), create a PMO H-item immediately — do not wait for session close. 2. Assign severity: RED (control/security/audit) / YELLOW (ops/integration) / GREEN (ecosystem/alignment). 3. Reference the evidence doc path + session. 4. rules.rule: Before extracting any SAP object, RESOLVE the extraction and analysis method via the method registry (brain_v2/method_registry.json or process_mining/method_registry.py). Do NOT rediscover how to read a SAP object each session by trial-and-error (RFC_READ_TABLE -> fails -> hunt the FM -> probe interface -> build). The registry maps: DD02L.TABCLASS -> method (TRANSP=RFC_READ_TABLE ROWSKIPS-free; POOL=RFC key-only+FM; CLUSTER=FOR ALL ENTRIES; VIEW=RFC_READ_TABLE) plus element overrides (RSAU=RSAU_API_GET_LOG_DATA chunk<=6h; SM21/ST22/SNAP=/USE/BL_GET_SHORTDUMPS; SOAMANAGER=unresolvable). Cross-link: claim #241, D_DATA, retro knowledge/session_retros/retro_operating_model_method_2026-06-21.md.
rules.why: Born 2026-06-21/22: every session we rediscovered extraction methods by trial (RFC_READ_TABLE -> fails -> hunt FM -> probe -> build). This is the #1 inefficiency identified in the operating-model retro. The registry is the fix: a resolver built from DD02L table class + hard-won element-specific overrides. Without it, a session wastes turns re-learning what RSAU requires chunked FM calls, what POOL tables return only keys, etc. Reference: process_mining/method_registry.py + brain_v2/method_registry.json (committed S-087).
rules.how_to_apply:
1. python process_mining/method_registry.py <OBJECT_NAME> -- returns (extract_method, constraint, analyze_method, retention)
2. If the object is in the Gold DB already, check sqlite schema first -- may not need re-extraction
3. For unknown tables, check DD02L.TABCLASS via RFC_READ_TABLE to get the type, then apply the type rule
4. Never RFC_READ_TABLE a CLUSTER table (fails silently or errors) -- use FOR ALL ENTRIES
5. Never 2-day RSAU call -- chunk <=6h or connection hangs
6. The registry is EXTENSIBLE: when a new override is discovered, add it to OVERRIDE dict in method_registry.py and re-run to regenerate brain_v2/method_registry.json

rules.rule: A claim with <2 independent evidence sources is WEAK. A single-source or surface-count finding is a HYPOTHESIS, not a finding. rules.rule: P01, D01, AND V01 RFC_READ_TABLE is wrapped by class SAIS which REJECTS ROWSKIPS with OPTION_NOT_VALID -- this is a LANDSCAPE-WIDE constraint, not a per-system quirk. This causes silent silent data truncation — not an error you see immediately. Use ROWCOUNT=0 with a tight WHERE partition (by FIKRS, date range, or other high-cardinality key) so each call stays manageable (there is NO ~60k platform ceiling: ROWCOUNT=0 returned 390,707 rows for BPGE in one call; partition is for memory/latency only). NEVER use ROWSKIPS-based pagination against P01/D01.
rules.why: Session s088 (2026-06-22): refresh_funds_from_live.py used ROWSKIPS pagination against P01 and silently returned only 30,000 of 56,639 UNES funds — a 47% data loss with no error raised. The failure mode is silent: SAIS returns OPTION_NOT_VALID internally but the caller gets a partial result, not an exception. This also applies to D01 (reference_d01_rowskips_and_adt_ddic_limits.md, s081). The method_registry.json already records this constraint ('P01-secured: NO ROWSKIPS') but no behavioral rule captured the SILENT TRUNCATION risk and the correct partitioning pattern. | s093 (2026-06-29): D01 ROWSKIPS rejection confirmed DIRECTLY on FM tables (FMFINCODE, FMFINT) via gap-analysis script. rc=5 OPTION_NOT_VALID — identical to P01. Prior D01 reference (s081) was for ADT/DDIC context; this is the first FM-table direct confirmation on D01. | s-2026-07-02: V01 ROWSKIPS rejection confirmed DIRECTLY on USR02/PA0001/PA0105 (extract_v01_actor_grounding.py, rc=5 OPTION_NOT_VALID) -- 3rd system confirmed, closing the class: assume EVERY system in this landscape rejects ROWSKIPS unless proven otherwise (claim #319).
rules.how_to_apply:
1. NEVER pass ROWSKIPS > 0 to RFC_READ_TABLE on P01 or D01. The call will appear to succeed with partial rows.
2. Instead: use ROWCOUNT=0 in a single call per partition. Partition by FIKRS for FM tables, by date range for event tables, by PSPID prefix for WBS.
3. Verify row counts against expected universe (e.g. compare with a COUNT(*) call or prior run): a result capped suspiciously near 30k means ROWSKIPS was used (no platform row ceiling exists for ROWCOUNT=0 — corrected s089).
4. For very large tables (hundreds of thousands of rows), partition by a secondary key (e.g. year, bukrs) for memory/latency — NOT because of a platform row ceiling.
5. Run `python process_mining/method_registry.py <TABLE>` to confirm the constraint before coding any extraction.
6. DEPRECATED: refresh_funds_from_live.py. Use scripts/extraction/p01_fm_ps_bcs_masterdata_refresh.py instead (claim #244).
rules.correction_note_s089: S-089 correction: the ~60k ceiling was false. BPGE returned 390,707 rows, FMBH UNES 248,086 rows in single ROWCOUNT=0 calls (confirmed via _gold_sync_log 2026-06-22). The earlier truncation was caused by explicit ROWCOUNT=30000 in the deprecated script, not a platform limit. Rule text updated.
rules.correction_note_s2026_07_02: Generalized to V01 (3rd confirmed system) 2026-07-02 during the unescrp actor-chain grounding extraction. Rule scope widened from P01+D01 to "this landscape" language; no behavior change, only evidence + wording.
rules.correction_note_s2026_07_02b: Related quirk on the SAME wrapper found during the follow-up V01 Funds+WBS extraction (extract_v01_funds_wbs.py, claim #321): this SAIS-wrapped RFC_READ_TABLE also raises TABLE_WITHOUT_DATA (not FIELD_NOT_VALID) when a requested FIELDNAME does not exist on the table -- indistinguishable from a genuinely empty result. Confirmed: FMFINCODE has no FIVOR field, PRPS has no PSTRT field. ALWAYS validate the field list against DDIF_FIELDINFO_GET before concluding a table is empty on this landscape.

rules.rule: When a bulk/delta extraction run completes without error, ALWAYS verify that the golden table row count approximately matches the P01 raw count for the same partition. A run that exits 0 CAN silently drop rows (e.g. via a key-collapse dedup on a table whose stored columns lack the full unique key). Do NOT dedup a line-item table unless the stored golden columns cover its FULL SAP unique key. For transaction tables (FMIOI, FMIFIIT, BSEG, etc.): check the DDIC key vs the golden column list before writing any dedup logic; if they differ, store ALL rows (no dedup) and use multiset-diff for delta.
rules.why: S-089 (2026-06-22): gold_refresh.py txn-partitioned engine deduped by all-non-amount columns. FMIOI has 13 golden columns but its SAP unique key includes a line counter NOT in the golden extract. Result: 1,813,943 rows silently collapsed to 1,029,062 (~43% loss) with exit code 0. Only discovered via manual raw-count comparison: P01 UNES 2025 = 806,902 raw but golden had ~405k for ALL institutes (impossible). Fixed in commit 8190f3c. See claim #247.
rules.how_to_apply: 1. After any extraction run: query P01 for COUNT(*) of the key partition and compare to golden row count. Allow <=0.1% variance for live churn (inserts/deletes between runs); >1% variance = re-investigate. 2. Before writing dedup logic for a table: run PRAGMA table_info(golden) to list golden cols, then check DD05L/DDIC key for the SAP table. If any key field is absent from the golden extract, do NOT dedup — store all rows. 3. For delta runs: use multiset diff (count occurrences of each full-row tuple) rather than set diff. 4. Verify FMIFIIT (ok: has FMBELNR+FMBUZEI+RLDNR+STUNR), BSEG (ok: BUKRS+BELNR+GJAHR+BUZEI), FMIOI (was broken: missing line counter in golden). 5. Add a post-pull assertion in the extractor: if n_total < 0.9 * expected_p01_count: HALT and report.

rules.rule: Never re-derive AVC availability from FM document tables (FMIFIIT/BPJA/FMAVCT WRTTP arithmetic at posting-leaf level). The ONLY correct AVC figure comes from FMAVC_READ_TOTALS_FOR_ADDRESS (standard FM chain) or report FMAVCR. Leaf-level arithmetic produces 23.7% spurious negatives because the control object is DERIVED AND ROLLED-UP via strategy AFMA (OPF budget aggregated at TC, not at the posting commitment item). Hand-rolling silently misses the rollup and the negative-at-parent budget distribution.
rules.why: committed_vs_available_detector.py was refuted empirically (s091): fund 196EAR4042 -> leaf arithmetic gave -$12.9M while V01 live FMAVC_READ_TOTALS_FOR_ADDRESS returned positive available. MBF fund: -$110M spurious negatives = 23.7% of active WBS. Root cause verified in ABAP source + config: strategy AFMA step 1 collapses all OPF commitment items to TC; leaf sum cannot reconstruct that rollup. This is the same class of error as GL balances from BSIS vs GLT0 (rule feedback_gl_balance_from_fs10n_not_bsis). Claims #253, #256, #259.
rules.how_to_apply: 1. For any AVC availability question: call FMAVC_READ_TOTALS_FOR_ADDRESS via RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN on V01 or D01 (not P01 -- S_DEVELOP needed). Or run report FMAVCR in V01/D01. 2. To check-only AVC without commit (e.g. reservation pre-flight): FMFR_CREATE_FROM_DATA with I_FLG_CHECKONLY=X. 3. Never compute available = SUM(budget) - SUM(consumed) per (fund, fundsctr, cmmtitem) from fmavct or fmifiit -- that is WRONG because the control object is a derived address, not the posting leaf. 4. The Gold DB fmavct_* slice only has ALLOCTYPE_9=KBFC rows (consumption); it cannot reconstruct available on its own without the budget base from FMAVC_READ_TOTALS_FOR_ADDRESS. 5. If ALL FMAVC_* FMs are not RFC-enabled (TFDIR FMODE=empty): confirm S_DEVELOP on the calling user on V01/D01, use RFC_ABAP_INSTALL_AND_RUN wrapper pattern.

rules.rule: When reconciling a fragment-assembled companion against its live HTML output, treat drift as BIDIRECTIONAL: (a) HTML-only blocks (present in the live companion but missing from fragments — port INTO the relevant fragment file); (b) fragment-only blocks (present in fragments but not yet rebuilt into the companion — DO NOT delete them; they merge correctly on the next rebuild). Never force byte-equality by discarding fragment-only content — that is an irreversible loss (CP-001). Reconciliation method: run --check → use difflib SequenceMatcher on newline-normalized lines → inspect BOTH insert-hunks (live-only) AND delete-hunks (fragment-only) → port on RAW bytes preserving CRLF+UTF-8 → verify no loss by diffing new built companion vs old → refresh MANIFEST baseline after confirming identity.
rules.why: Session 2026-06-30 (commit 5bcb07a): the BCM Structured Address companion (companions/BCM_StructuredAddressChange.html) was ~21 KB short of the live companion. --check via build_bcm_structured_address_companion.py revealed three drift blocks: Block 1 = HTML-only CITI/CGI Dbtr+Cdtr analysis (+23,437 B across 181 lines) that existed in the live companion but never made it back into tabs/25_phase0.html; Block 2 = a missing leading emoji on a Phase 4 h3 in tabs/29_phase4.html; Block 3 = a fragment-only section (Citi test-tool 2026-06-26, brain claims #265/266/267) present in tabs/29_phase4.html but not in the companion because rebuild had never been re-run after that edit. The failure mode: a naive 'port everything from live to fragments' approach would have silently deleted Block 3 content. CP-001 requires treating every fragment-only hunk as intentional until confirmed redundant.
rules.how_to_apply:
When --check reports a size/hash mismatch on a fragment-assembled companion:
1. Run the builder with --check to get difflib hunk output (or equivalent).
2. Classify each hunk: INSERT = live-only (missing from fragments); DELETE = fragment-only (missing from live).
3. INSERT hunks: identify the correct fragment file (by tab/section name) and port the raw bytes into it, preserving CRLF+UTF-8.
4. DELETE hunks: DO NOT remove them from fragments. Verify they are not already present elsewhere; if truly new, they will merge into the companion on rebuild.
5. Rebuild the companion and confirm the new live file matches the expected content.
6. Compare new vs old companion to verify no content loss in either direction.
7. Refresh the MANIFEST.json baseline (byte_count + sha256 + sha256_lf) ONLY after confirming byte-identical integrity.
8. Never update the MANIFEST baseline to the pre-reconciliation state — only update after the full reconciliation is clean.
rules.cp_link_reason: CP-001 'Knowledge over velocity': the fragment-only content represents work already done (brain claims #265/266/267 analysis) that would be irreversibly deleted if the reconciler only read one direction of the diff. Velocity would suggest 'just make the fragments match the live companion'; CP-001 demands inspecting what the live companion is missing too. The bidirectional check is the minimum-loss path.

rules.rule: Before loading budget (or any master/transactional value) into a target system, READ the target's existing state at that EXACT key first -- an idempotency check, not just a presence check. If a value already exists at that key, NET-CHECK before posting (do not just add a new line), because most SAP posting APIs (e.g. BAPI_0050_CREATE for BCS budget) are additive, not upsert -- posting again at an already-populated key creates a double, not a correction.
rules.why: Session 2026-07-06: 14 cost-recovery funds were loaded into V01 without first reading V01's existing state at the target (fund, fund center, commitment item) key. V01 already had budget at CI-11/13 for 11 of the 14 funds, so the new ENTR/B1 posts doubled the budget rather than establishing it. Compounded by an earlier mis-addressing in the same session (loading at commitment item TC, then at fund center HEQ, both wrong for this batch per claim #338) -- three separate write-without-verify-first mistakes on the same batch. Reversal was blocked (reversal reasons not active for FY2026 in both D01 and V01, claim #324), forcing a negative-offset BAPI_0050_CREATE workaround (claim #325) to net the doubles/mis-addresses back to zero -- extra cleanup work that a pre-write read would have avoided entirely.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. Identify the EXACT key the write targets (for BCS: fund + fund center/FISTL + commitment item + fiscal year + ledger/version -- not just the fund).
2. Read the target system's live state (FMBL/FMAVCT for budget; the equivalent master/transaction table for any other domain) at that exact key BEFORE posting anything.
3. If a value already exists at that key: NET-CHECK (compare the source value against what's already there) -- do not blindly add. If the API is additive (most BAPI_0050_* budget posts are), compute the delta needed and post only the delta (or the negative-offset if you already over-posted).
4. Never assume a target starts empty just because the source system has the value -- targets used for prior testing/dev work commonly already carry partial or full state.
5. This generalizes the 'verify before alarming / verify by re-read' family (feedback_verify_before_alarming_and_update_on_correction) to the WRITE side: verify BEFORE you write, not just before you report.
rules.cp_link_reason: CP-003 'Precision, evidence, facts': writing to a target system without first reading its current state at the exact key is an unverified assumption (the target is empty / the target matches the source), not a checked fact. The fix is the same discipline CP-003 already demands for claims -- verify before asserting -- applied to the write path instead of the report path.

rules.rule: Audit parallel worktree branches at session start AND close. A commit that lives only on a `.claude/worktrees/<name>` branch is invisible to `git status`/`git log` on your own branch and is NO safer than uncommitted work -- gone if the disk dies. Durability = the work is on ORIGIN, not merely 'committed'.
rules.why: Session 2026-07-07: the worktree branch `unruffled-williamson-810b11` @5285e92 held the entire AVC recurring-pipeline layer -- 5 claims, gold_table_registry +266 rows, a capability-model bump, and the new 330-line scripts/extraction/psm_avc_refresh.py -- committed but never merged or pushed. Nothing on the active feature branch or origin referenced it; it was one disk failure from total loss. This is the concrete mechanism behind the measured weakest capability, DURABILITY (0.233): 'I committed' felt safe but the work was stranded locally.
rules.how_to_apply:
1. At session start and close run: `git worktree list`; for each worktree HEAD `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> HEAD || echo STRANDED`; and `git log --oneline origin/<branch>..HEAD | wc -l` for unpushed on the current branch.
2. Any tip NOT an ancestor of a pushed branch = stranded knowledge -> merge it, preserve-first (union; on a claim/record id collision, keep the earlier-referenced side's ids and RENUMBER the other, then fix its citations -- both branches took claim ids 304-308 here, AVC renumbered to 341-345).
3. Never treat a local commit as durable. Push before you consider the work captured.
4. Prune only fully-merged worktrees, and only when no parallel session is using one (no active-work.md lease).
rules.cp_link_reason: CP-002 'Preserve first, context is cheap': stranded local commits are the failure mode where hard-won knowledge is silently at risk of irreversible loss. Preserving it means making it durable (on origin) and merging without clobbering, not just leaving it 'committed somewhere'.

rules.rule: Before answering ANY scope question -- which SAP modules/components exist, what is actually used, how UNESCO operates, what the integrations are -- READ brain_v2/system_profile/unesco_system_profile.json (it is rendered at the top of BRAIN_INDEX.md at bootstrap). NEVER re-derive the footprint from cvers/audit logs inside a conversation. Always separate INSTALLED vs CONFIGURED vs PRODUCTIVE.
rules.why: s097 (2026-07-28): an external Business-Process-Review questionnaire was answered by re-deriving the footprint live. RE-FX, SD, FI-AA, PM and TRM were all reported as 'not implemented / not evidenced' -- all five are PRODUCTIVE (RE-FX alone: 312 contracts, 1,600 rental objects, 6 custom packages). An entire category was missing: third-party add-ons (EPI-USE Labs on HCM, ACL Data Link extracting daily, Winshuttle installed-dormant) -- two of which are independent DATA-EXIT channels, i.e. directly material to a data-governance answer. Root cause: executed_objects_domain_map has no bucket for RE-FX nor for /EPIUSE/, /ACLDL/, /WINSHTLQ/, /GBX01/, so 40% of execution volume sits in 'Uncatalogued' -- and absence-in-the-map was read as absence-in-the-system. The user had to catch the same class of error twice in one session.
rules.how_to_apply: 1) Read the profile FIRST; it is the base fact-sheet of the tenant. 2) If the profile lacks the answer, probe P01 read-only and WRITE THE RESULT BACK into the profile -- never leave a new fact in the chat. 3) Never infer 'not implemented' from absence in executed_objects_domain_map or from a table missing in the Gold DB: both are FLOORS, not inventories. Say 'not evidenced -- to confirm' and probe. 4) State INSTALLED vs CONFIGURED vs PRODUCTIVE explicitly; 177 components are installed and most ship by default.

claims.claim: AVC available is a fund/cover-group level metric, not an FR-line-level metric. All FR lines on the same (FONDS, FUNDSCTR, CMMTITEM-rolled-to-control-object) draw from a single shared AVC pool. The pool is calculated as: Available = FMAVCT.allotment - sum(open FMIOI commitments) - sum(FMIFIIT actuals) on the same key. FMAVC005 fires when Available <= 0 + new posting amount > 0. The triggering FR line is incidental; the constraint is the fund pool.

claims.claim: Root config that PERMITS the FM-PS model gap (TIER_1 from fmavct_2026): UNESCO's AVC derivation rule FMAFMAP013500109 (env 9HZ00001) collapses 8 of the 9 operational FIPEX (11, 13, 20, 30, 40, 50, 10\' and REVENUE) into a SINGLE control object called TC. Only PSC (FIPEX 80) keeps its own separate control object. Therefore the AVC engine validates against only 2 buckets per fund (TC + 80) instead of the 9 FIPEX visible in FMIFIIT. The TC bucket includes REVENUE in its pool, so as long as REVENUE > sum(operational consumption), TC stays positive and AVC permits postings — even though individual operational FIPEX are deeply negative. AVC is structurally blind to per-FIPEX deficits because it never sees them. UNESCO-wide pattern: 6,550 control objects use TC aggregator out of ~9,500 FMAVCT_2026 rows = ~80% of fund-FundCenter combinations are vulnerable to this exact pattern. Two root-config fixes: FIX-G1 (modify FMAFMAP013500109 so each FIPEX has its own control object — granular AVC) or FIX-G2 (keep TC aggregation but exclude REVENUE from the pool). Either is ~1 sprint config + UAT — cheapest structural fix yet identified, alternative to FIX-E/F.

claims.claim: INC-000008088 Treasury interest GL split is constrained by an architectural invariant: bank statements can only be re-routed to specific GLs when the bank emits a SPECIFIC external transaction code (e.g. NINT — Normal Interest) that distinguishes interest from other credits. Banks that emit only GENERIC codes (NTRF, NCHK, NCLR) for ALL credit lines — including interest — CANNOT be split because there is no signal in the MT940 to tell SAP which credit is interest versus a regular transfer. At UNESCO, only Societe Generale exposes NINT reliably; all other Treasury HQ banks (BNP-Paribas, CIC, CRCAM, Banque Populaire, Citibank, Standard Chartered, Northern Trust BFM/HED, etc.) use generic NTRF for interest credits. Therefore the final implementation of INC-8088 splits ONLY the SOG banks (Group A → 7044013 via existing INTEREST_REC mask redirect; Group B → 7044014 via NEW SOG_FRB + 111B + INTEREST_REC_B). Group C (ASHI/Nessim) and Group D (PFF) remain on 7044011 as a known limitation, accepted by Treasury (M. Spronk validated 2026-05-05). The original architectural plan (TR_TRNFA/B/C/D + SOG_FRA + 111A/B/C/D + INTEREST_REC_A/B/C/D — 4-way clone) is OBSOLETE.

If a GL is not in any IF block, FundCenter stays SPACE and the posting fails with 'No funds center entered/derived in item XXXXX (UNES/<HKONT>/)'. **Any change that introduces a NEW HKONT into the EBS / FI posting chain at UNESCO MUST be paired with adding that HKONT to ZXFMDTU02_RPY** or the posting will be rejected. claims.claim: WBS PS-budget channel is GUI-only (CJ30/KBPP family) — no clean single-call RFC equivalent. KBPP_EXTERN_UPDATE raises DA300 NOT_FOUND without the full CJ30 buffer/profile context even with IMP_CHECK=X. Custom Y*BUDGET* FMs are readers/loggers only; BAPI_BUS2054_SET_STATUS = status only; BAPI_0050_CREATE = FM fund-center object (OBJNR FS*), NOT WBS (OBJNR PR*). WBS budgeting is a TWO-STEP process: (1) CJ30 sets the original/current budget → stored in BPJA as WRTTP=41 (current budget); (2) CJ32 releases it → stored in BPJA as WRTTP=42 (released budget). Budget is ANNUAL (table BPJA by GJAHR), NOT overall (BPGE WRTTP=01 was empty for WBS 650RER0008 / OBJNR PR00021132). Corrects the earlier '0 budget in P01' which only checked BPGE/overall — BPJA WRTTP=41 (GJAHR=2026) had the 10,000 USD entry. BPGE WRTTP=01 = overall-level; BPJA WRTTP=41 = annual current; BPJA WRTTP=42 = annual released; VERSN=000 throughout. Budget-exceeded message = BP/604 (PS-AVC engine, not FM-AVC). RESOLVED s-2026-07-01 (was open — see KU-2026-CJ32-RELEASE-NOT-LANDING, now closed): PS-AVC/BP-604 checks the RELEASED budget WRTTP=42 (set by CJ32), NOT the original/current WRTTP=41 (set by CJ30). Proof: WBS 650RER0008 (OBJNR PR00021132) has WRTTP=41=10,000 USD for FY2026 but WRTTP=42=0, and BP/604 still fires on a posting attempt — the WRTTP=41 entry alone does not satisfy AVC. Therefore CJ32 release is MANDATORY, not just CJ30; the two-step CJ30→CJ32 sequence is a hard AVC precondition, not merely bookkeeping.

claims.claim: Cost-recovery WBS carry 0 PS-budget in BPGE on BOTH P01 and D01 (verified: 650RER0008 = 0 BPGE rows WHERE OBJNR LIKE PR*). Spendability of CR WBS comes from the FUND-level budget (633CRP9003, OBJNR FS*, claim #268/#287), NOT from a WBS-level PS-budget entry. Therefore a BP/604 (PS-AVC budget-exceeded) on a CR WBS in D01 signals a PS-AVC profile CONFIG DIFFERENCE (D01 has PS-AVC active; P01 relies on FM-AVC fund-level coverage for CR objects), not genuinely missing budget. claims.claim: RFC_READ_TABLE reads of wide tables on P01 (such as FMAVCT with 77 fields / 38-col schema) require field-split batching: split columns into groups of <=7, RFC-read each group, recombine by row position with an equal-rowcount guard (assert all groups return the same number of rows). This is necessary because RFC_READ_TABLE has a 512-byte WA (work area) buffer and returns BUFFER_OVERFLOW beyond that limit. P01 also rejects ROWSKIPS (SAIS restriction -- claim #244); workaround = ROWCOUNT=0 partitioned by RFIKRS x RYEAR. Pattern implemented in scripts/extraction/psm_avc_refresh.py; reuse for any future wide-table RFC extraction from P01.
claims.resolution_notes: Reusable tooling pattern. The 512-byte WA buffer is a known RFC_READ_TABLE constraint; this documents the working workaround tested against P01 FMAVCT. Cross-link: claim #244 (P01 SAIS ROWSKIPS rejection). Script: scripts/extraction/psm_avc_refresh.py.

evidence_for.cite: Field-split implementation: FMAVCT 77 fields split into <=7-col groups; each RFC-read; recombined by position; guard: assert all groups same row count. ROWCOUNT=0 per RFIKRS x RYEAR avoids ROWSKIPS. Tested live P01: 18,838 rows FY2024 / 16,112 FY2025 / 13,593 FY2026 -- all cross-split counts match.

claims.claim: THREE LAYERS, NOT ONE (s097). Keying domains on SAP modules (FI, CO, MM, SD) conflates a TECHNICAL taxonomy with a business one: nobody in an organisation does 'FI', they pay an invoice or commit a budget, and every such act crosses several modules. Worse, `_module_to_domain` was ONE-TO-ONE and cannot be — FI-BL-PT pays suppliers (P2P), staff (payroll), travellers and treasury deals; PSM-FM serves B2C2A, P2P commitment checking, POST2BUDGET and PROJ2FUND. The model now separates COMPONENT (SAP's taxonomy, deterministic, not ours to rename) / DOMAIN (who owns it) / FLOW (what the organisation does end to end), with MANY-TO-MANY edges between all three. DECISION: do NOT rename domains to component codes — that would make a business layer look technical. Add the flow layer instead. PROCESS MINING RUNS ON FLOWS, never on modules, which is exactly why every vendor ships content named P2P/O2C/R2R. PUBLIC-SECTOR FLOWS WITH NO MARKET CONTENT: B2C2A (budget→commitment→actual, the primary financial control, FMRESERV 6.4M change docs), POST2BUDGET (position budgeting, 68 users), PROJ2FUND (PS 1.6M execs), GRANT2REPORT (no capability at all).

claims.claim: ALGORITHMS ARE NESTED, not a flat list (s097, user insight). An algorithm's output is another's input: this is a directed graph with layers. L0 INVARIANT (component resolution, anchored on SAP itself) -> L0b CUSTOM OVERLAY (Z/Y objects, which SAP cannot resolve by definition) -> L1 OBSERVATION (logs, classification) -> L2 BOUNDARY (interface discovery, which PRODUCES the satellite catalogue) -> L3 ORIGIN (satellite derivation + the two-axis engine) -> L4 FLOW (process mining, per flow) -> L5 CONFORMANCE (needs a flow AND a normative model) -> L6 SELF-CHECK. THREE CONSEQUENCES: (1) an algorithm cannot be better than its dependencies — A3's origin resolution is capped by F1's parse quality; (2) improving a LOW layer lifts everything above it, measured: the L0 fix took the frontier from 40% to 7.7% without touching anything above; (3) the improvement mechanism must weight by DEPTH, which it does not yet.
